feed.title: NPR Topics: World
feed.subtitle: NPR world news, international art and culture, world business and financial markets, world economy, and global trends in health, science and technology. Subscribe to the World Story of the Day podcast and RSS feed.

entry.title: Alberta voters decide whether to take a step toward separating from Canada
entry.summary: In Canada, the oil-rich province of Alberta votes in a referendum that could set it on a path toward separation, as Prime Minister Mark Carney warns of threats to Canadian unity.

entry.title: Australian prime minister says lawmaker critically injured by car is 'no accident'
entry.summary: A car hit an Australian federal independent lawmaker on Monday, critically injuring her in an apparent deliberate attack, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said. The driver was arrested.

entry.title: 2026 midterms could be the most expensive on record. And, Macron condemns protests
entry.summary: More than $15 billion has been raised in this year's midterm elections. And, France's president is condemning the violent protests erupting across the country.

entry.title: Ukraine and Russia exchange strikes, as relations between Trump and Zelenskyy sour
entry.summary: Ukraine carried out a massive drone strikes on Russia, which launched deadly attacks on its smaller neighbor over the weekend.

entry.title: Solar power is changing agriculture in Pakistan, but some fear it could cause issues
entry.summary: Solar power is transforming agriculture in Pakistan. But in a country already facing water scarcity and extreme weather, some fear their widespread use could cause problems.

entry.title: Alberta voters weigh future in Canada
entry.summary: On Monday voters in the oil-rich Canadian province of Alberta are deciding whether to take the first step toward a future referendum on independence.

entry.title: Trump endorses embattled Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for reelection
entry.summary: Trump said in a post on social media that Netanyahu "has been a Great Warrior Prime Minister, and an even greater Partner for Peace in combatting the Islamic Republic of Iran."

entry.title: Political rivals implicated under Pakistan's anti-terror law
entry.summary: Pakistan's political showdown continues as more opposition figures are implicated under Pakistan's anti-terror law.

entry.title: 'Life is absolutely brutal in Gaza,' says World Food Programme head
entry.summary: The UN's World Food Programme says 1.4 million people in Gaza are suffering acute food shortages and that funding gaps are forcing cutbacks in critical aid, despite the U.S. brokered Hamas-Israel ceasefire.

entry.title: Ukraine and the U.S. are at odds over Starshield. Here's what to know
entry.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said he believes the U.S. government is behind his military's loss of normal access to the key satellite communications service used by the Ukrainian military.
